clauses.text:
(1) to permit officers and employees of 
the Social Security Board, Federal Se­
curity Agency, upon recommendation of 
the Board and approval of the Federal 
Security Administrator, to hold office 
under state, territorial, and municipal 
governments engaged in cooperative and 
related work with the Social Security 
Board, as authorized by Federal and 
State laws: Provided, that the services 
to be performed by them shall pertain to- 
such work and shall not in any manner 
interfere or conflict with the perform­
ance of their duties during their regular 
hours of duty as officers or employees of 
the Federal Government; and (2) to 
permit state, territorial, and municipal 
officers or employees engaged in cooper­
ative and related work with the Social 
Security Board, unless prohibited by law, 
to accept appointment in and serve 
under the Social Security Board, Fed­
eral Security Agency, when the Board 
and the Administrator deem such em­
ployment necessary to secure a more 
efficient administration of the duties 
imposed upon the Social Security Board: 
Provided, that the appointment of any 
such officer or employee to a position 
subject to civil-service laws under the 
Social Security Board shall be made in
accordance with civil-service laws, rules, 
and regulations.

eral Security Agency, when the Board

ployment necessary to secure a more

versions.research_rationale: Executive Order 8399 (official Federal Register text, 5 FR 1607, PDF pages 1-1, read in the saved OCR text layer of the govinfo issue PDF: heading, enacting clause, operative text and signature/filing line are all present) permits (1) Social Security Board officers and employees, on the Board's recommendation and the Federal Security Administrator's approval, to hold state, territorial and municipal office in cooperative work with the Board, and (2) state, territorial and municipal officers in such work to serve under the Board. Its whole operative content is an amendment of Executive Order No. 9 of January 17, 1873, as amended (the 1989 OFR disposition table: 'Amended EO 9'; 'Revoked by EO 11408'). EO 11408 of April 25, 1968 (33 FR 6459, saved official text read in full) revoked EO 9 itself in section 1 and in section 2 revoked 'All prior Executive orders insofar as they interpret or amend Executive Order No. 9'; EO 11408 section 2 names it expressly in its list of revoked amendatory orders. Because the order consists only of that amendment, 'insofar as' reaches all of it, which is also why the OFR catalog's '(in part)' qualifier on some of these notes does not leave any part in force. EO 11408 states no effective date, so the revocation took effect on signing, 1968-04-25. The order has no expiry, condition or temporary term, the OFR catalog and the saved-text corpus show no earlier amendment or revocation, and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches show no current citation. However, the order names the Social Security Board, which was abolished in 1946, so an earlier cessation is possible and the first end is not asserted (see gap); EO 11408's revocation is recorded as a later event. Partial claim: original text, clause inventory, savings and later-source search are asserted; the ending is not. OCR quotations keep the scan's recognition errors (and soft hyphens) exactly as held; they have not been compared with page images.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 11408 contains no savings, transition or continuation clause. Its section 1 revoked Executive Order No. 9 of January 17, 1873 (the dual federal-state office-holding prohibition) itself, and section 2 revoked every prior order insofar as it interpreted or amended that order. This order's only operative content is an amendment of (an exception to) that 1873 order, so once the prohibition itself was revoked nothing remained for the exception to operate on, and no office, fund, property, entitlement or enforceable right was created by the order that could survive; office-holding done under the permission before 1968 was lawful when done and is a completed historical fact, not a continuing effect.
